answer: Graph factorization is described as scalable to large networks because it learns low-dimensional representations by factorizing a graph-related matrix, which can be done efficiently with linear or near-linear methods and avoids expensive operations on the full graph. Its main graph-type restriction is that it is typically formulated for simple, undirected graphs, so it does not directly handle directed or multi-relational graphs without modification.
